Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FUEL TAP FOR MOPEDS 



1. Scope — Covers basic requirements and dimensions of fuel tap used in mopeds. 

2. Definitions 

2.1 Fuel Tap — A mechanical device meant to allow/check the passage of fuel. In the case of 
mopedSj the fuel is a mixture of petrol and oil as recommended by the manufacturer [ see also 
IS : 4639-1968 Glossary of petroleum terms ]. 

3. Shape and Dimensions 

3.1 The recommended shape and dimensions of the fuel tap are as shown in the figure given 
below. A tell-tale indication shall be provided on or in the vicinity of the fuel tap indicating the 
operating positions of lever. 



FILTER 




RESERVE TUBE 




M12xl,LH 
(TOP HALF) 

M12X 1,RH 
(BOTTOM HALF) 




OUTLET 
NIPPLE 



All dimensions in millimetres. 

3.2 The minimum length of the operating lever shall be 25 mm. 

3.3 The outlet nipple dimensions shall be as shown in figure above, 

4- Material — The material used for the manufacture of fuel tap shall be aluminium, brass or zinc 
base die casting alloy. The recommended materials for other conrponents are as follows :

5. General Requirements 

5.1 A mechanism shall be provided to operate the tap in three different directions as shown below : 

RESERVE 



OFF 



v*y 



OFF 



ON 

5.2 The minimum fuel flow rate through the tap under 100 mm head shall be 150 cc/minute. 

5.3 The minimum reserve capacity shall be 0*5 litre. 

5.4 The mesh size of filter element shall be 75 micron as per IS : 460 ( Part I )-1978 * Wire Cloth 
test sieves ( second revision ) '. 

5.5 The fixing arrangements of a fuel tap to the fuel tank may vary. 

6. Tests 

6.1 There shall not be any leakage of fuel from fuel tap assembly, under a minimum head of 
500 mm of fuel. 

6.2 The tap operating lever mechanism shall be tested in all the positions for 15 000 cycles and 
there shall not be any leakage of fuel under 500 mm head after the test. 

7. Marking 

7.1 The fuel tap shall be marked with the 

a) Manufacturer's name and trade-mark ( If any ), and 

b) Serial number and the year of manufacture. 

7.1.1 ISI Certification Mar A/ng — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

2 



IS: 10331 -1982 

9. Sampling 

9A Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the sampling inspection 
shall be carried out according to the procedure given in IS : 2500 ( Part I )-1973 'Sampling 
inspection tables : Part I Inspection by attributes and by count of defects \ The sampling plan to 
be followed for the different characteristics shall be as given in 8.1.1 and 8.1.2. 

8.1.1 For visual and dimensional characteristics, the single sampling plan with inspection 
level IV and AQL of 2'5 percent given in Table 1 and 2 of IS : 2500 ( Part I ) shall be followed. 

8.1.2 For the various tests given under 4.1 the sampling plan with inspection level II and AQL 
1 percent given in Table 1 and 2 of IS : 2500 shall be followed.
